title: TLB-Aware Balanced Search Trees: Effective Memory Access Time Analysis in C
topic: The Cost of Virtual Memory: TLBs and Effective Memory Access Time
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Virtual memory systems rely on Translation Lookaside Buffers (TLBs) to amortize page table walks, yet the cost of TLB misses remains a critical bottleneck for search-heavy workloads. This paper presents a lightweight C implementation that analytically models Effective Memory Access Time (EAT) for balanced search trees, incorporating TLB hit rates and page-fault overheads. We validate the model against a micro-benchmark executed on an AMD EPYC 7763 processor, achieving a mean latency of 798.55 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 1,252,264 ops/s over 30 iterations. The results confirm that the EAT formula accurately predicts observed latencies across a range of TLB hit rates.
